about.title: Halal compliance made clearer, more practical, and more accessible.
about.body: AHC Resources helps restaurants, cafes, bakeries, caterers and food manufacturers prepare for Malaysia Halal Certification through practical systems, documentation and audit readiness.

disclaimer.title: Independent guidance. Clear boundaries.
disclaimer.body: AHC Resources is an independent private halal consultancy. We assist with compliance preparation, documentation, training, gap assessments and application support. We do not issue or approve Malaysia Halal Certificates, and we do not guarantee certification approval.

halalIntro.lead: The Arabic word halal means permitted, lawful, or allowed according to Islamic law (Shariah). Its opposite is haram, meaning prohibited.
halalIntro.body: For food businesses, halal is more than checking whether an ingredient is permissible. It also covers the source, processing, handling, storage, preparation and protection from contamination with prohibited substances.

tayyib.title: Halal and tayyib
tayyib.body: The Qur'an connects halal with tayyib: good, wholesome, pure and beneficial. Food should be safe, clean and fit for consumption.

good.title: Lawful and good
good.body: Islamic food requirements bring together religious permissibility and wholesomeness, not one without the other.

source.title: Source matters
source.body: Prohibited foods and methods of obtaining food are clearly identified. The source and method by which food becomes food matter.

governance.title: Sound governance
governance.body: Halal and haram are established through legitimate Islamic sources, not personal preference or unnecessary restriction.

halalIntro.principlesSummary: Why these four halal principles matter
halalIntro.industrySummary: See how halal applies across the food industry
halalIntro.definition: Halal is anything that is permitted and lawful according to Islamic Shariah. For food, halal also requires the product to be wholesome, pure and safe (tayyib), with its ingredients, processing, handling and supply chain managed according to Islamic requirements.
halalIntro.industryIntro: Halal means that a product complies with Islamic requirements throughout its relevant supply chain and production process.
industryItems: Raw materials: ingredients must be halal.
Animal origin: animal-derived ingredients must come from permissible sources.
Slaughtering: applicable animals must be slaughtered according to Islamic requirements.
Processing: prohibited substances must not be used or introduced.
Equipment: production equipment must be controlled to prevent contamination.
Storage: halal products must be protected from non-halal contamination.
Transportation: handling and transport must maintain halal integrity.
Cleaning and sanitation: appropriate procedures must be implemented.
Packaging and labelling: information must not be misleading.
Traceability: the business should demonstrate where materials came from and how the product was produced.
halalIntro.references:
Al-Baqarah 2:168 — Consume what is halal and tayyib.
Al-Baqarah 2:172 — Eat the good provisions Allah has provided.
Al-Ma'idah 5:3 — Major categories of prohibited food.
Al-Ma'idah 5:87-88 — Do not prohibit what Allah has made lawful.
An-Nahl 16:114 — Eat the good and lawful provisions.

complianceRisk.title: Protecting your premises' halal certification.
complianceRisk.intro: Obtaining a Malaysian Halal Certificate is an important milestone for any food business. Maintaining certification requires continuous compliance with the applicable Malaysian Halal Certification requirements.
complianceRisk.context: A certified food premises may face non-compliance, suspension, withdrawal or termination when significant requirements are not maintained or when issues affect the halal integrity of the operation. AHC Resources helps businesses identify potential risks early and strengthen their halal compliance systems.
complianceRisk.riskSummary: View the eight common risk areas
complianceRisk.riskTitle: What can put certification at risk?

ingredients.title: Ingredients and raw materials
ingredients.body: New materials without appropriate supporting halal documentation can create compliance concerns.

suppliers.title: Supplier changes
suppliers.body: Changing suppliers without reviewing and maintaining the required documentation creates supply-chain risk.

operations.title: Premises or operations
operations.body: Changes to the address, production area, processes, products, brands or operations may require action.

documentation.title: Documentation gaps
documentation.body: Incomplete, outdated or inconsistent records make halal controls difficult to demonstrate.

audit.title: Inspection or audit findings
audit.body: Unresolved non-conformities and weak corrective action can affect certification status.

system.title: Halal management system
system.body: Weak implementation, monitoring or record keeping can create continuing compliance concerns.

logo.title: Certificate or logo misuse
logo.body: Improper use, alteration or misuse may result in enforcement action.

shariah.title: Shariah concerns
shariah.body: Handling, processing, storage or other practices may affect halal certification integrity.

certificates.question: Does AHC Resources issue halal certificates?
certificates.answer: No. We are an independent private consultancy. Certificates are issued by the relevant halal certification authority.

guarantee.question: Can you guarantee my halal certificate?
guarantee.answer: No. We help businesses prepare and improve compliance before applying, but the final assessment and approval remain with the relevant authority.

myehalal.question: Can you help with MYeHALAL?
myehalal.answer: We can provide preparation and application assistance within the scope permitted for a private consultant.

smallRestaurants.question: Do you work with small restaurants?
smallRestaurants.answer: Yes. Our support can be tailored to the scale and complexity of your business.
